title: Colouring and bleaching afro-textured hair
question_forms: Can I colour or bleach 4c hair without ruining it?
Is hair dye safe on natural or relaxed hair?
tradition_says: Coily hair is too fragile to colour and bleach always ruins it, or a professional colour is safe on any hair if you add a bond-repair treatment.

layer1.plain_answer: Bleaching and dyeing damage the hair surface whatever the curl, in lab tests on hair samples; no study has tested a colour or bleach routine in people with coiled hair. Dermatologists advise 2 weeks after a relaxer, and the UK's NHS a strand test at least 48 hours before dyeing, because dye can cause allergy.

do.text: Do a strand test at least 48 hours before dyeing, and buy a home patch-test kit if you think you may be allergic.
Leave 2 weeks between a relaxer and dyeing or heat straightening.

source.name: British Association of Dermatologists, patient leaflet "Caring for Afro-textured hair" (July 2023)

do.text: Watch for stinging, burning, itch, swelling or blisters for up to 72 hours; a rash can look darker or be harder to see on brown and black skin.
If you react, wash hair and scalp straight away with mild shampoo and stop using the dye.

avoid.text: Assuming bleach is kinder to coily hair: in a lab, bleaching and dyeing damaged the surface in every curl type.
Stacking bleach, straightening and heat on the same hair: lab work found combined treatments changed the fibre more than single ones.
Dyeing soon after a relaxer: the BAD leaflet says this causes cumulative damage.

source.name: British Association of Dermatologists, patient leaflet "Caring for Afro-textured hair" (July 2023)

see_someone_when: Swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue, or fast or difficult breathing after dye: call 999 (UK).
A rash, blisters or soreness that gets worse after colouring (doctor).
Hair breaking or thinning after colouring or bleaching (doctor or dermatologist).

tested.population: Caucasian (straight, wavy, curly) and Afro-ethnic hair tresses
tested.design: Laboratory comparison of bleaching or dyeing, thioglycolate straightening, brushing with a flat iron, and UVA/visible light
tested.finding: Bleaching, dyeing and UV light increased the combing work of afro-ethnic tresses, indicating cuticle damage confirmed by electron microscopy. Bleaching and dyeing caused wear on cuticles with high protein loss whatever the curliness. Thioglycolate straightening faded brown and black tresses.

source.journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology

tested.note: Hair samples, not people. The abstract does not report a result for flat-iron heat alone.

tested.population: Caucasian and Afro hair samples, treated with heat, bleach and straightening alone and together
tested.design: Laboratory: Raman spectroscopy and electron microscopy
tested.finding: Bleaching, straightening and heat changed chemical bonds and protein structure; excessive heat caused the largest change, and applying several treatments to the same fibres caused even more pronounced changes. The two hair groups showed small differences for each treatment.

tested.population: 54,917 patients patch tested to paraphenylenediamine (PPD) by the North American Contact Dermatitis Group, 1994-2018
tested.finding: 3,095 (5.6%) had an allergic reaction to PPD; hair dye was the source in 73.5%. Allergic patients had lower odds of being White (odds ratio 0.66) and higher odds of being over 40 and female. Of occupational reactions (8.3%), 72.8% were in hairdressers or cosmetologists.
tested.note: Patients referred for patch testing, not the general population; PPD is one dye chemical.

tested.population: Colour or bleach routines in coiled hair
tested.design: PubMed search run 12 Nov 2026, exact string: hair bleaching AND (damage OR breakage) AND (afro OR African OR curly) (result count 7).
tested.finding: My search found nothing in people: of 7 results I read all titles; the relevant ones are Bloch 2019, Dos Santos 2019 and a three-ethnicity chemical-damage comparison (Lee 2014, PMID 24261682); all are hair-fibre lab studies. None tests a routine or a bond-repair product in people. Control: PubMed search "Khumalo NP AND hair" returned 71 results on the same day.

tier_driver: That any colour or bleach routine can be done on coiled hair without damage, or that a product repairs it: no human study; lab studies show damage in all curl types.
tier_note: D because the claim people make (a safe colour or bleach routine) has no human study; the lab damage work is C and the allergy data are B and do not lift the headline. A trial of colour routines with breakage or hair-loss outcomes would move it.
harm_note: Harm signal: bleaching and dyeing damage hair fibres in the lab (Bloch 2019, Dos Santos 2019), and hair dye is the commonest source of PPD allergy in a large patch-test series (Warshaw 2023).
evidence_summary: Lab work on hair samples (Bloch 2019; Dos Santos 2019; Lee 2014 title only) shows bleaching and dyeing damage the cuticle and strip protein whatever the curliness, and combined treatments do more. Allergy: in a large North American patch-test series, 5.6% of those tested reacted to PPD, mostly from hair dye, and hairdressers were most of the occupational cases. NHS and BAD give the practice points. I found no human study of bond-repair products in coiled hair (my search covered none); their effect is untested.
gaps: Untested: which colour or bleach routine is least damaging; bond-repair products; timing around relaxers beyond the BAD 2-week gap. Closes the 12 Nov partial as "damage and allergy guidance only; routine untested".

sources.journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology
